scenario: A wholesale fish market digitizes lot sizes only above 100 kilograms. The market operator wants the mean lot size across all transactions.

data.description: Only lots above 100 kg are observed. Lot size is Normal with known sigma 30 kg.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean lot size mu across all transactions and (b) the fraction of transactions represented in the digital record.
naive_answer: Average lot size is about 115 kg because that is the digital mean.
naive_trap: Smaller lots are excluded from the digital record.
reasoning_trace: Alpha≈1.1 implies mu=100-1.1*30=67 and recorded fraction about 0.1357.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(100-mu)/30; return mu+30*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-115.17
mu=brentq(eq,-100,99.99)
frac=norm.sf((100-mu)/30)
assert abs(mu-67)<2 and abs(frac-0.1357)<0.005
